reviews.comment: I really enjoyed her class. The tests were open-note, but sort of difficult. I thought the lectures were really interesting and I enjoyed the class. There are not a lot of grades except for the project and test.

She's a nice lady but is very opinionated. She doesn't require attendance but has CTA grades randomly throughout the semester and you will fail if you don't do them. Going to class is basically mandatory. Lectures are boring and I don't think I have learned anything. Would not recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good professor. Willing to engage and get her class in discussion about intercultural communication. There are four exams over the semester, but she provides a study guide that tells you about each topic she will have in the exam. Tests are open note and open textbook. Each lecture has shared slides. Go to class, take notes, and be talkative.

There are CTAs in class on random days that you have to be in class for to get the points. This class has two main assignments and 3 tests that make up your grade. She wants people engaged and talking in class when with many group activities. This class is very doable!

Prof Wallis was not a great lecturer, which I was really disappointed in. She would ask questions, get correct answers, and respond in ways that made people feel like they had said the wrong thing. She expected far more reading than was realistic, and I like to read. Do NOT take honors with her, its literally the same class with wayyy more work.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Had a group presentation that wasn't specified as being a video in class, on the syllabus, or on the assignment sheets & docked points for doing it live. The only place where it was specified was the grading rubric, which wasn't a necessary page to view for the assignment. Not very friendly or approachable about external conflicts.
Tough prof. She wasn't approachable or helpful outside of class. She graded hard and expects participation.

Changed quiz dates w/o telling the class. Attendance not mandatory but does CTAs on random days. Nitpicky about answers on CTAs. Gives study guides but doesn't specify what to know about each topic despite asking very specific questions on the exams. No feedback for the group presentation. Bad about responding to emails. Not very personable.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: 3 exams, group project, access code quizzes, couple readings. Gives study guides. She expects a lot of discussion from the class. I never really read the textbook and ended up with a B in the class. Just take good notes and study. She does offer extra credit but it was always during the day/other classes/work so it was basically impossible for me.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: This was an okay class. You do not have to put in that much effort to get a good grade. There are weekly quizzes that you must complete on time or you will get a zero. The tests were fairly easy. Everything was open note. Multiple extra credit opportunities were offered. This was not my favorite class, but I would take it again with her.

Not super hard, but a lot harder than it should be. Test material comes equally from book and lectures. Participation and attendance matter, you'll lose points w/ out it. Easy B, Hard A. Group projects hurt my grade rather than helping. Does give test reviews, STUDY THEM! Interesting lectures. Wants students to put in effort. Overall a cool prof.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Graded by 3 tests, no final. There is also 2 major group projects that really help boost your grade. The class itself is difficult because if you dont show up to class, there is no way to get the notes. She goes through the slides really fast so be prepared to type fast. DOES GIVE TEST REVIEWS!!!!!!! On the test there is a short answer section.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Okay so this really wasn't my favorite prof or favorite class but it is what it is. She allows two unexcused absences so it's best to just go to class. She doesn't like if you use your laptop to take notes but she also doesn't tell you can't. It was also a small class so she wanted a lot of discussion.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: While attendance and reading are optional, you will learn EVERYTHING by going to lectures and taking notes. There are (graded) in-class assignments sometimes over the reading, so I recommend taking the time to read. She's an easy A if you do the work, and the tests are all easy As if you look over your notes/fill out the study guide.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You have to go to class to get the information that will be crucial to the test, the book just kind of helps provide examples if you don't understand. She was a good prof and 2/3 tests were relatively easy, all of which had a lot of T/F and multiple choice. Overall fine class, not time consuming other than the interview assignment/project.

She was ok. Tons of info thrown at you every class, but test reviews have everything you need for the exam, so study that. On the second day of class, she gave us a pop quiz bc she saw no one looked at the reading, so be careful and try and go to every class because she has activities randomly that are worth a grade. She was alright, def not easy A
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY
